extraction.Name: Mrs. Walter Ten Fingers—nee Emma Gillispie
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee at the time it was issued, September 29, 1919, as she did not want to pay taxes on her 160 acre allotment; but that she was informed that, if she did not take the patent in fee, and keep her taxes up, the placed would be taxed just the same, and later sold for taxes, so she accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1921, she sold her place to Oliver Swallow, of Oelrichs, South Dakota, for $1000.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: Oliver Swallow, of Oelrichs, South Dakota, for $1000.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she paid no taxes out of this, if taxes were paid for this laid during the two years she held patent over it, the purchaser evidently paid them
extraction.Occupation/Income: she personally receives annually $30.00 lease money, from heirship land; and that this salary of her husband's and her lease money constitutes their entire income
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent; health is not very good; mother of two children, minors, and one of the girls is nearly blind; husband from a former marriage has five minor children which he supports, in addition to her and her two children; husband and his five children have good health; husband is a policeman on the Pine Ridge Reservation for the United States Government; did not sell her place for any debts incurred prior to receiving the patent in fee; never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; allotment described as 160 acres, considered very poor land; affidavit sworn March 18, 1929, Shannon County, South Dakota
